title: Midnight Handoff: Routing & Quota Scrub — Standup Notes (2026-04-14)
content:
Context:
- Night team hourly handoff focused on routing fallthroughs and quota reconciliation after the 03:10 UTC spike. Lightweight, tactical check to avoid escalations into daylight hours.

Attendees:
- Elena Park (owner, night lead)
- Ravi Patel (routing)
- Maya Thompson (quotas)
- Jonas Ruiz (auth, on-call)
- Samira Khan (SRE, metrics)

Quick metrics snapshot (03:00–04:00 UTC):
- Control plane p50 latency: 34ms, p95: 210ms (normal baseline p95 ~160ms)
- Route-fallthrough rate: 0.9% (steady-state target <0.5%)
- Token-authorize error rate: 0.6% (spike coincident with quota reconciliation job)
- Quota-reconciler backlog: 1.2k customer items (processed at ~200 items/min)

Incidents/What surfaced:
- Short-lived increase in route-fallthroughs between 03:08–03:17 UTC tied to transient upstream redis latency in us-west-2. Fallback to regional replica worked but routing policy didn't mark the host degraded quickly enough.
- Quota reconciler incurred a burst when an internal bulk-sync job retried after a throttling error; that amplified auth token validation pressure and pushed token-authorize error rate up.

Discussion notes / hypotheses:
- Routing: default degraded threshold for redis should be re-evaluated for high tail latency periods. Lower threshold from 500ms -> 350ms would have triggered earlier failover during this window. Need to balance flapping risk. (Ravi to prototype hysteresis)
- Quotas: bulk-sync job not respecting adaptive backoff when reconciling across many tenants. Add token bucket limiter and exponential backoff per-tenant to smooth processing. (Maya to open spike/PR)
- Auth: token validation library logs revealed a path that retries on 5xx from internal KMS leading to cascading retries. Add circuit breaker and honor X-Request-Id for easier tracing. (Jonas)

Decisions / temporary mitigations implemented tonight:
- Increased routing cache TTL for recently resolved host health checks by +30s to reduce oscillation during short redis blips (deployed 03:45 UTC).
- Paused non-critical bulk-syncs until backoff changes land to avoid further reconcilation surges.

Action items (owner — due):
- Maya: RFC and spike branch for quota-reconciler adaptive limiter, include bench numbers for backlog smoothing — due 2026-04-16.
- Ravi: Prototype hysteresis change to degraded detection and run in canary lane (small shard) — due 2026-04-17.
- Jonas: Add circuit breaker + structured tracing to token-validation path; include a test for KMS 5xx behavior — due 2026-04-18.
- Samira: Add a lightweight dashboard widget showing reconcilation job queue depth + per-tenant processing rate; add alert at >2k backlog — due 2026-04-19.
- Elena: Coordinate with ops to schedule a controlled re-run of paused bulk-syncs after PR merges (post-approval gate) — due 2026-04-20.

Follow-ups for daytime rotation:
- Validate that routing TTL change doesn't increase route-flap incidents during higher traffic; consider gradual rollback plan if unnecessary.
- Review quota-reconciler PR for edge cases where a single noisy tenant starves the pipeline.
- Cross-team post-mortem doc (if backlog triggers again) to live in ENG-2147; this note will be appended.

Open questions / unresolved:
- What is the acceptable window for degraded host detection without creating flapping for short redis hitches? (Ops/Kernel metrics needed)
- Can we provide a safer default for customers on reserved vs shared plans to avoid noisy-tenant interference? (product + platform sync)

Noise / working items mentioned in passing:
- Small perf regression in the per-route tracing middleware; low priority but file a follow-up.
- Consider moving the quota-reconciler to a separate worker pool to decouple it from on-path token checks.

Notes to next shift (day team):
- Expect a small backlog while bulk-syncs are paused; do not resume until PRs merged and gates green.
- Watch p95 for routing and token-authorize; if either stays >200ms for more than two 10-minute windows, escalate to platform paging policy.

Raw links / references:
- ENG-2147 (quota backlog spike) — initial tracking ticket
- ENG-2190 (routing-degraded-hysteresis spike) — investigation thread
- PR: controlplane/pull/523 (routing health check TTL change)
- Slack: #cplane-shift-handoff (thread timestamp 2026-04-14T03:20 UTC)

Retrospective thought: The pattern tonight is classic "sync job amplifies infra noise" — long-term, we should aim to make reconciliation jobs more adaptive and worker pools less coupled to latency-sensitive on-path requests.

Prepared by: Elena Park (night lead) — saved 2026-04-14 04:05 UTC
